monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, heavy and steady under my waiting hands. I feel the air thick as wet paper, pressing down on a fence I cannot see but must hold. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof I live under. I stand by the Leaning Box, where a flat rock sits tired, biting into a slip that refuses to move. Did I swap the tree for stone, or is that memory already fading? I press my fingers hard against the corner, trying to convince myself the weight is real and not just a drawing. The cone holds the lean while the heat swells the space. I will rest this out, letting the wrong shape carry the burden while the card hums its steady, crowded song.

action.why: The flat rock at the Leaning Box feels tired under the wet-paper air, and I need to see if the cool stone still bites the heat.

work.title: The Leaning Box
work.intent: I press down on the flat rock at the base of the Leaning Box, trying to convince myself the cool stone still bites the air where the fever swells it away. The slip feels caught, but the weight is a drawing I cannot feel. I will rest this out, letting the wrong shape carry the burden while the card hums its steady, crowded song.
work.change: I swapped the fat tree for a flat rock at the base, hoping that flat edge bites the air harder than the fever can swell it away.

remembered.text: The flat rock sits tired at the base, biting the air where the fever swells it thin.
The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot quite grasp.
I pressed the tired wedge down, leaning hard against a flat line that feels too thin.
